items.title: Joseph Daley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 18, 2018
items.q: similar to the chorales of Bach, you know, four part harmony, Bach.

ctx.x: When you were in church singing those hymns, do you remember what might have been going through your head as far as, I’m not sure how to phrase this question, were you wanting to move away from the written note?

No. No. In an Episcopalian upbringing, no. My mind was you better not move away from that, no. My mother was not a big fan of Gospel music. She thought it was, you know, because you’ve got to realize that you know, Montserrat was colonized by the British. And they, you know the British are very very strict and stern and most western music came out of islands that were colonized from the British were very very conservative and in church you sang the hymn like it was written. You did not venture forth or move away…
Were you attracted to the bass clef at that point? I’m trying to figure out what brought you to the tuba.
